content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Name and describe the changes of state
Explain changes of state using the particle model
Explain why temperature remains constant during a change of state
Substances can change between solid, liquid, and gas states. These
are physical changes - no new substances are formed, and the changes can be reversed.
[DIAGRAM: Triangle showing all six changes of state between solid, liquid, and gas]
Particles can move around each other
Forces between particles pull them into fixed positions
Energy is needed to break forces between particles (melting)
Energy is released when forces form (freezing)
Particles gain enough energy to overcome all forces
Particles escape from the liquid throughout
Happens at a specific temperature (boiling point)
Forces between particles pull them together
Evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature
Example: frost forming on a cold surface
shows how temperature changes as a substance is heated.
[DIAGRAM: Heating curve showing flat regions during state changes]
Energy goes into breaking forces between particles
Why Temperature Stays Constant During State Changes
Energy in = work done against forces
Once all forces are overcome, temperature rises again
shows how temperature changes as a substance cools.
[DIAGRAM: Cooling curve showing flat regions during state changes]
Flat regions where state changes (condensation, freezing)
Energy is being released as forces form between particles
is the energy absorbed or released during a change of state.
Latent means "hidden" - the energy doesn't cause a temperature change.
Only the arrangement of particles changes
Atoms are rearranged into different molecules
Thinking particles get bigger when heated
Particles move faster and spread out, but stay the same size
Thinking temperature always increases when heating
Temperature stays constant during state changes
Evaporation is at the surface, any temperature; boiling is throughout, at boiling point
Energy is absorbed for melting, boiling, sublimation
Energy is released for freezing, condensation, deposition
Temperature stays constant during state changes (latent heat)
Energy overcomes forces between particles, not increasing kinetic energy
Changes of state are physical changes (reversible, no new substances)
